# beachrain

**Does rain affect my beach?** `beachrain` helps Sydney swimmers see whether bacteria levels at their beach tend to rise after rain and how their beach compares with other nearby beaches.

**Documentation website:** <https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-abhignatippala/>

## What's in the package

| Component | What it does |
|---|---|
| `beach_samples` | 36,062 enterococci samples from 77 Sydney swim sites (2015 to 2025), each matched to the rain that fell in the previous 72 hours |
| `sydney_rainfall` | Daily Sydney rainfall and temperature used to build the 72-hour totals |
| `summarise_exceedance()` | Share of samples above a bacteria threshold in each rainfall band |
| `compare_sites()` | Ranks swim sites by how much rain changes their water quality |
| `plot_exceedance()` | Bar chart of a beach's summary beside its region |
| `run_app()` | Launches the *Rain Check* Shiny app |

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/YOUR-REPO-NAME")
```

## Launch the app

```r
library(beachrain)
run_app()
```

The app is designed for Sydney swimmers who want to know how rain might affect their usual beach. Choose your beach and the bacteria level you want to check. The chart then shows how your beach (blue) compares with other beaches in the same region (beige) across four different levels of rainfall.


## A quick example

```{r example}
library(beachrain)

bondi <- beach_samples[beach_samples$swim_site == "Bondi Beach", ]
summarise_exceedance(bondi, threshold = 40)
```

Compare `prop_exceed` in the Dry row with the Heavy row: the gap shows how
much heavy rain raises the chance of poor water quality at Bondi.

## Data

- **Water quality:** Beachwatch NSW, NSW Government,
  <https://www.beachwatch.nsw.gov.au/waterMonitoring/waterQualityData>
- **Weather:** Open-Meteo historical weather API, licensed under CC BY 4.0,
  <https://open-meteo.com/>

Both datasets were curated for
[TidyTuesday (20 May 2025)](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2025/2025-05-20)
by Jen Richmond (R-Ladies Sydney). The script `data-raw/beach_samples.R`
downloads the raw files and reproduces the package data.
